def test_post_boundary_activation_refusal_is_required(self):
        phases = self._phases()
        manager = {"before": self._snapshot(10, "i1", "boot-1"),
                   "after": self._snapshot(11, "i2", "boot-1"),
                   "after_phase": {"direct": {"rc": 0},
                                   "dependency": {"rc": 1}}}
        reboot = {"before": self._snapshot(11, "i2", "boot-1"),
                  "after": self._snapshot(12, "i3", "boot-2"),
                  "after_phase": {"direct": {"rc": 1},
                                  "dependency": {"rc": 0}},
                  "boot_id_before": "boot-1", "boot_id_after": "boot-2",
                  "qemu_pid_before": 99, "qemu_pid_after": 99,
                  "qemu_identity_verified": True}
        checks = vm.build_checks(phases, manager, reboot)
        self.assertFalse(checks["mask_persisted"])
evidence.reason: At the pinned tip the test remains one combined case: manager restart has direct rc 0/dependency rc 1 while reboot has direct rc 1/dependency rc 0, followed by a single assertFalse(mask_persisted). It never starts with all post-boundary activations refused and flips one return code at a time. An implementation that omitted an individual refusal, especially the reboot dependency case, could still pass this test. This is a minor test-coverage defect, not a requirement expansion.
